publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Parvalbumin-positive interneurons of the prefrontal cortex support working memory and cognitive flexibility

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether one class of prefrontal interneuron accounts for all of the behavioural consequences of prefrontal dysfunction, or only some
span.quote: Although these disturbances all appear to involve PFC dysfunction, it is unclear whether specific circuit elements within the PFC contribute differentially to symptom complexity.

span.label: which PFC-dependent behaviours require intact parvalbumin interneuron output, and which survive its loss
span.quote: To distinguish PFC-dependent behaviors which require intact PVI signaling from those that do not, we compared PVI-selective interference with non-cell-type-selective perturbations of the same circuitry in behavioral assays that were chosen to detect alterations that map onto symptom categories (positive, negative, cognitive) in schizophrenia.

span.label: shows that silencing PV interneurons reproduces the cognitive deficits of a whole-region lesion but none of the social or psychostimulant ones, so a composite syndrome maps onto separable circuit elements
span.quote: By sampling for behavioral alterations that map onto distinct symptom categories in schizophrenia, we show that dysfunction of PVI signaling in the PFC specifically produces deficits in the cognitive domain, but does not give rise to PFC-dependent correlates of negative or positive symptoms.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: By sampling for behavioral alterations that map onto distinct symptom categories in schizophrenia, we show that dysfunction of PVI signaling in the PFC specifically produces deficits in the cognitive domain, but does not give rise to PFC-dependent correlates of negative or positive symptoms.

span.label: prefrontal parvalbumin interneuron control of working memory and cognitive flexibility
span.quote: Thus various modalities of PFC-dependent working memory critically depend on PVI integrity.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: To directly test how chronic impairment of PVI signaling affects PFC-dependent behavior, we selectively blocked output from PVIs in the mouse PFC by cell-type- and region-selective expression of tetanus toxin light chain (TeLC).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: PV interneurons generate the fast network oscillations that synchronise prefrontal and coupled circuits, and that synchrony is what supports information processing during working memory — so blocking PV output removes it
span.quote: Generation of network oscillations in turn is thought to depend on the activity of fast-spiking putative PVIs

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Loss of glutamatergic prefrontal afferent control dysregulates ventral brainstem dopamine neurons, raising subcortical dopamine and hence amphetamine sensitivity after PFC lesion
span.quote: Consistent with this idea, lesions of the PFC in rodents also increase amphetamine sensitivity and subcortical dopamine presumably through dysregulation of dopaminergic neurons in the ventral brainstem after loss of glutamatergic PFC afferent control

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A division of labour among GABAergic interneuron sub-populations means silencing only the PV class removes one specific circuit function, producing a cognitive-only deficit profile rather than the full lesion profile
span.quote: In contrast, selective inactivation of one sub-population of GABAergic interneurons – PVIs – caused deficits only in the cognitive domain, suggesting that these interneurons may subserve specific circuit functions in the PFC.

span.label: tetanus toxin light chain is expressed only where Cre flips its reading frame, and it stops release by cleaving VAMP2
span.quote: As Cre-recombinase is required to flip the reading frame into the correct orientation, transcription of TeLC can only occur in PVIs 26 . Once expressed, TeLC efficiently stops transmitter release by cleaving VAMP2, a protein required for synaptic vesicle docking

span.label: PV interneurons target the soma, proximal dendrites and axon initial segment of principal cells, which is why they can govern regional output
span.quote: In the isocortex PVIs mainly comprise basket and chandelier cells, which control network activity by targeting the soma and proximal dendrites or the axon initial segment of principal cells, respectively

span.label: the proposed route from PV loss to cognitive deficit runs through network oscillations, which are thought to depend on fast-spiking interneurons
span.quote: At the systems level synchronous network activity within the PFC and across functionally coupled brain structures may aid information processing during working memory 56 , 57 . Generation of network oscillations in turn is thought to depend on the activity of fast-spiking putative PVIs

span.label: the route from prefrontal damage to amphetamine hypersensitivity runs through loss of cortical control over subcortical dopamine
span.quote: It is thought that both positive symptoms and increased amphetamine sensitivity are due to enhanced subcortical dopaminergic tone, which in turn correlates with and might be secondary to PFC dysfunction in schizophrenia

span.label: impaired PV signalling may be where many separate genetic and environmental risks converge
span.quote: Accordingly impaired signaling of PVIs may form a common endpoint for different genetic and environmental factors leading to PFC malfunction and schizophrenia-associated deficits

span.label: The two manipulations (viral silencing and lesion) were run as separate sequential experiments, so the four groups cannot be compared in a single factorial analysis.
span.quote: This experimental design precludes a direct 2 × 2 statistical comparison.

span.label: A small fraction of transgene expression fell in PV-negative cells, whose identity is inferred rather than established.
span.quote: Transgene-expression in PV-negative cells was scarce (4.3%) and likely includes PVIs containing PV levels below detection threshold.

span.label: Viral expression was verified quantitatively in only one of the two water-maze cohorts.
span.quote: Only cohort 1 was quantitatively assessed (n = 10/17).

span.label: silencing covers over 75% of PV cells, not all of them, so a residual population remains active
span.quote: Bilateral infusions of AAV-FLEX-TeLC resulted in expression of TeLC in over 75% of PVIs in prelimbic and infralimbic regions of the PFC

span.label: VAMP2 immunoreactivity was reduced but not abolished; completeness of the block is argued from a previous result in a different brain region
span.quote: The residual VAMP2 immunoreactivity is likely due to low affinity recognition of VAMP2 cleavage products by the antibody 31 . However, using the same AAV-FLEX-TeLC we have previously shown that transmission of hippocampal PVIs was fully abolished 10 days after virus injection despite residual VAMP2 immunoreactivity

span.label: 4.3% of transgene expression was in PV-negative cells, which the authors read as PV below detection rather than off-target
span.quote: Transgene-expression in PV-negative cells was scarce (4.3%) and likely includes PVIs containing PV levels below detection threshold.

span.label: in the water maze only one of two cohorts was quantitatively verified histologically; the rest was confirmed by eye
span.quote: Water maze experiments were replicates of two cohorts. Only cohort 1 was quantitatively assessed (n = 10/17). For cohort 2 and all PFC-PV-GFP animals correct viral expression was confirmed visually.

span.label: the reversal deficit after PV silencing is transient, so the manipulation delays rather than prevents relearning
span.quote: Analysis of reversal performance by subject revealed that this deficit was transient in PFC-PV-TeLC animals, where all mice eventually acquired the new location.

span.label: the tripartite positive/negative/cognitive symptom division, imported as a way of choosing which rodent assays to run
span.quote: To distinguish PFC-dependent behaviors which require intact PVI signaling from those that do not, we compared PVI-selective interference with non-cell-type-selective perturbations of the same circuitry in behavioral assays that were chosen to detect alterations that map onto symptom categories (positive, negative, cognitive) in schizophrenia.

span.label: tetanus toxin light chain, used as a genetically targetable silencer of transmitter release
span.quote: As Cre-recombinase is required to flip the reading frame into the correct orientation, transcription of TeLC can only occur in PVIs 26 . Once expressed, TeLC efficiently stops transmitter release by cleaving VAMP2, a protein required for synaptic vesicle docking

span.label: amphetamine-induced locomotion as a behavioural proxy for subcortical dopamine tone
span.quote: It is thought that both positive symptoms and increased amphetamine sensitivity are due to enhanced subcortical dopaminergic tone, which in turn correlates with and might be secondary to PFC dysfunction in schizophrenia

span.label: PFC
span.quote: Compared with controls, PFC-Lesion animals showed significantly higher levels of locomotor activity ( Fig. 6F ), with increased peak activity ( p = 0.04; t = 1.97) and slower decay kinetics ( p = 0.005; t = 3.25), confirming the importance of the PFC for amphetamine sensitivity.

span.label: amphetamine
span.quote: Compared with controls, PFC-Lesion animals showed significantly higher levels of locomotor activity ( Fig. 6F ), with increased peak activity ( p = 0.04; t = 1.97) and slower decay kinetics ( p = 0.005; t = 3.25), confirming the importance of the PFC for amphetamine sensitivity.

span.label: PFC dysfunction is used at two different grains here - a whole-region lesion and the loss of one interneuron class - and the paper's point is that they are NOT the same manipulation
span.quote: We found that PFC lesions produced behavioral alterations in all three symptom categories, whereas selective inactivation of PVIs caused deficits only in the cognitive domain.

span.label: working memory in this paper spans three tasks with different demands: repeat investigation, spontaneous alternation, and a 60s delayed match-to-place
span.quote: we used a delayed (60s) match-to-place test in a Y-maze configuration in the water maze, where the percentage of correct responses in match trials represents trial unique short-term memory

span.label: cognitive, negative and positive symptoms are used as ANIMAL CORRELATES of clinical categories, assigned by which behavioural assay was chosen
span.quote: To distinguish PFC-dependent behaviors which require intact PVI signaling from those that do not, we compared PVI-selective interference with non-cell-type-selective perturbations of the same circuitry in behavioral assays that were chosen to detect alterations that map onto symptom categories (positive, negative, cognitive) in schizophrenia.

span.label: mouse PFC here means a block spanning prelimbic, infralimbic, cingulate and medial orbital cortex, treated as integrating what three separate human regions do
span.quote: Additionally, TeLC expression was found in the cingulate and medial orbital cortices, demonstrating functional removal of PVIs across an area of mouse PFC thought to integrate functions of the dorsolateral, medial and orbital PFC in humans

span.label: inactivation means blocked transmitter release with the cell alive, not cell death - the contrast case in the same paper kills the tissue
span.quote: As Cre-recombinase is required to flip the reading frame into the correct orientation, transcription of TeLC can only occur in PVIs 26 . Once expressed, TeLC efficiently stops transmitter release by cleaving VAMP2, a protein required for synaptic vesicle docking

span.label: builds-on → the authors' own earlier study of hippocampal parvalbumin interneurons using the same AAV-FLEX-TeLC construct (cited as ref. 26)
span.quote: However, using the same AAV-FLEX-TeLC we have previously shown that transmission of hippocampal PVIs was fully abolished 10 days after virus injection despite residual VAMP2 immunoreactivity 26 .

span.label: extends → post-mortem findings of reduced GAD67 and parvalbumin in schizophrenia
span.quote: In particular reduced mRNA levels of the 67 kD isoform of the GABA synthesizing enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67) have been consistently reported 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 . These changes seem to dominantly affect a subclass of GABAergic interneurons, that expresses the calcium-binding protein PV, which itself shows reduced expression in schizophrenia

span.label: confirms → prior lesion work establishing PFC involvement in social behaviour and amphetamine sensitivity
span.quote: Compared with controls, PFC-Lesion animals showed significantly higher levels of locomotor activity ( Fig. 6F ), with increased peak activity ( p = 0.04; t = 1.97) and slower decay kinetics ( p = 0.005; t = 3.25), confirming the importance of the PFC for amphetamine sensitivity.

span.label: qualifies → the view that PV interneuron pathology explains the breadth of prefrontal dysfunction in schizophrenia
span.quote: In summary, impaired signaling of PVIs in the PFC, which is thought to form a core pathology in schizophrenia, may be causally involved in the development of cognitive symptoms. However, amphetamine-hypersensitivity and deficits in social-approach avoidance behavior as indicators of positive and negative symptoms, respectively, are not precipitated by PVI dysfunction. Based on these data we suggest that different aspects of the composite symptomatology of PFC dysfunction in schizophrenia can be allocated to specific neuronal elements.

span.label: supports → bicuculline studies in which total disinhibition of the PFC reproduced the full lesion-like profile
span.quote: Interestingly, complete disruption of GABA A -receptor-mediated inhibition in the PFC by bicuculline infusion has been shown to cause similar behavioral alterations as those we report here for PFC-lesion animals

span.label: distinguishes-from → somatostatin interneurons, silenced the same way with no working memory effect
span.quote: Such a “division of labor” scenario between different populations of interneurons is further supported by our finding that analogous tetanus toxin-based targeting of a different, somatostatin (Sst)-expressing, population of interneurons in the PFC of Sst-Cre mice 71 caused no change in working memory performance in the same task that was clearly impaired after inactivation of PVIs

span.label: tetanus toxin light chain —causes→ VAMP2
span.quote: As Cre-recombinase is required to flip the reading frame into the correct orientation, transcription of TeLC can only occur in PVIs 26 . Once expressed, TeLC efficiently stops transmitter release by cleaving VAMP2, a protein required for synaptic vesicle docking

span.label: basket —is-a→ PVIs
span.quote: In the isocortex PVIs mainly comprise basket and chandelier cells, which control network activity by targeting the soma and proximal dendrites or the axon initial segment of principal cells, respectively

span.label: chandelier cells —is-a→ PVIs
span.quote: In the isocortex PVIs mainly comprise basket and chandelier cells, which control network activity by targeting the soma and proximal dendrites or the axon initial segment of principal cells, respectively

span.label: tetanus toxin light chain —contrasted-with→ ibotenic acid
span.quote: We reasoned that this approach would confirm the PFC-dependence of our behavioral tests and that qualitative comparison of the behavioral deficits between PV-cell-selective and non-cell-type-selective circuit lesions would allow us to dissociate general PFC functions from those that specifically involve PVIs.

span.label: PVIs —contrasted-with→ somatostatin
span.quote: Such a “division of labor” scenario between different populations of interneurons is further supported by our finding that analogous tetanus toxin-based targeting of a different, somatostatin (Sst)-expressing, population of interneurons in the PFC of Sst-Cre mice 71 caused no change in working memory performance in the same task that was clearly impaired after inactivation of PVIs

span.label: PVIs —causes→ working memory
span.quote: Thus various modalities of PFC-dependent working memory critically depend on PVI integrity.

span.label: PVIs —causes→ Behavioral flexibility
span.quote: In contrast, during reversal, PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice needed more time to learn the new platform location although this was only significant for PFC-PV-TeLC mice (PFC-PV-TeLC vs. PFC-PV-GFP, day effect F(3,84) = 24; p < 0.001; group effect F(4,84) = 8.8; p = 0.006; and PFC-Lesion vs. PFC-Saline, F(3,60) = 2.1; p = 0.16)

span.label: PFC —causes→ social preference
span.quote: Accordingly social approach/avoidance behavior as well as social recognition memory/novelty preference depends on the PFC circuitry. PV-positive interneurons, however, do not seem to be a crucial component of this circuit.

span.label: RETRACTED (NOT A RELATION) · PFC —causes→ amphetamine
span.quote: Compared with controls, PFC-Lesion animals showed significantly higher levels of locomotor activity ( Fig. 6F ), with increased peak activity ( p = 0.04; t = 1.97) and slower decay kinetics ( p = 0.005; t = 3.25), confirming the importance of the PFC for amphetamine sensitivity.

span.label: PFC —distinct-from→ spatial reference memory
span.quote: During initial training PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice learned the platform location as well as their respective controls as indicated by the reduction in path length (PFC-PV-TeLC/PFC-PV-GFP, day effect: F(4,120) = 45; p < 0.0001, no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1; PFC-Lesion/PFC-Saline, day effect: F(4,80) = 28; p < 0.0001; no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1) ( Fig. 4A,B ; see also Fig. 5 ) and the amount of time spent in the target quadrant during probe trials ( t’s < 1.4) ( Fig. 4 insets in A,B), indicating that spatial reference memory per se does not depend on the PFC

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · match-to-place —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.quote: we used a delayed (60s) match-to-place test in a Y-maze configuration in the water maze, where the percentage of correct responses in match trials represents trial unique short-term memory

span.label: hole-board —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.quote: We implemented a hole-board-based working memory test by analyzing repeat investigations of previously explored holes.

span.label: amphetamine —operationalised-as→ positive
span.quote: It is thought that both positive symptoms and increased amphetamine sensitivity are due to enhanced subcortical dopaminergic tone, which in turn correlates with and might be secondary to PFC dysfunction in schizophrenia

span.label: RETRACTED (NOT A PART-OF RELATION IN EITHER DIRECTION) · GAD67 —part-of→ schizophrenia
span.quote: In particular reduced mRNA levels of the 67 kD isoform of the GABA synthesizing enzyme glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD67) have been consistently reported 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 . These changes seem to dominantly affect a subclass of GABAergic interneurons, that expresses the calcium-binding protein PV, which itself shows reduced expression in schizophrenia

span.label: RETRACTED (THE OPERATIONALISATION POINTS THE WRONG WAY) · match-to-place —operationalised-as→ working memory
span.quote: To assess whether PVIs also contribute to temporally expanded forms of working memory, which are known to be impaired after PFC lesions 40 , 41 , we used a delayed (60s) match-to-place test in a Y-maze configuration in the water maze, where the percentage of correct responses in match trials represents trial unique short-term memory 26 .

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Unless otherwise stated data were analysed with two-tailed paired or unpaired Student’s t-test as appropriate.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: We also used two-way ANOVA with treatment as between-subject and trial/day as within-subject factors.

span.label: chi-squared / Fisher's exact test
span.quote: Contingency analysis applied Fisher’s exact or Chi-Square tests.

span.label: significance level (alpha)
span.quote: The null hypothesis was rejected for alpha greater than 5%.

span.label: spectral power analysis (Fast Fourier Transform)
span.quote: Artefact free continuous recordings (120s) of LFPs were chosen and spectral power analysis conducted using Fast Fourier Transform in BrainVision Analyzer 2.0 software

span.label: t
span.quote: As expected, immunoreactivity for VAMP2 was strongly reduced in TeLC-positive terminals of PFC-PV-TeLC mice when compared with GFP-positive terminals of PFC-PV-GFP mice ( p < 0.0001; t = 22.2; n = 4 animals per group;

span.label: day effect
span.quote: During initial training PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice learned the platform location as well as their respective controls as indicated by the reduction in path length (PFC-PV-TeLC/PFC-PV-GFP, day effect: F(4,120) = 45; p < 0.0001, no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1; PFC-Lesion/PFC-Saline, day effect: F(4,80) = 28; p < 0.0001; no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1) ( Fig. 4A,B ; see also Fig. 5 ) and the amount of time spent in the target quadrant during probe trials ( t’s < 1.4) ( Fig. 4 insets in A,B), indicating that spatial reference memory per se does not depend on the PFC

span.label: Fast Fourier Transform
span.quote: Local field potentials (LFPs) from PFC were recorded while animals were freely moving in their holding cage. Low weight dummies were removed and replaced by a wireless data logger for continuous recording of 4 channels and on board memory (NeuroLogger, New Behavior, Zurich, Switzerland), set at a sampling rate of 200 Hz.

span.label: Silencing PV interneurons in the prefrontal cortex produced deficits only in the cognitive domain, whereas non-selective PFC lesions disrupted behaviours mapping onto all three schizophrenia symptom categories.
span.quote: We found that PFC lesions produced behavioral alterations in all three symptom categories, whereas selective inactivation of PVIs caused deficits only in the cognitive domain.

span.label: Both PV-silenced and lesioned mice reinvestigated previously explored holes more often than their controls, despite equal overall nose-poke numbers.
span.quote: both PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion animals showed increased levels of repeat investigations

span.label: Spontaneous alternation in the Y-maze was reduced in both PV-silenced and lesioned mice relative to controls.
span.quote: ( C ) In the same cohorts of mice spontaneous alternation in a Y-maze is reduced in PFC-PV-TeLC animals and in ( D ), PFC-Lesion animals compared to respective controls.

span.label: In the 60-second delayed match-to-place task control mice improved significantly on match trials while PV-silenced mice did not, so temporally extended working memory also requires PV interneurons.
span.quote: Whereas PFC-PV-GFP animals showed significant improvement in match trials, PFC-PV-TeLC animals did not ( Fig. 3E ).

span.label: Initial water-maze acquisition was normal in both PV-silenced and lesioned mice, indicating spatial reference memory itself does not depend on the PFC.
span.quote: During initial training PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice learned the platform location as well as their respective controls as indicated by the reduction in path length

span.label: Reversal learning was impaired in both manipulations, but PV-silenced mice eventually reached criterion while over 30% of lesioned mice never did, so the PV deficit is transient and the lesion deficit persistent.
span.quote: However, whereas PFC-PV-TeLC mice met reversal criterion upon overtraining, more than 30% of PFC-Lesion mice failed to do so.

span.label: Lesioned mice failed to discriminate a familiar from an unfamiliar conspecific, whereas PV-silenced mice showed normal sociability and social recognition.
span.quote: In contrast PFC-Lesion animals did not discriminate between familiar and unfamiliar mice

span.label: Amphetamine produced hypersensitivity — higher peak locomotion and slower decay — in lesioned mice only.
span.quote: Both groups show enhanced locomotor activity after receiving amphetamine but PFC-Lesion animals show a hypersensitivity as indicated by increased peak locomotor activity (inset) and slower decay kinetics.

span.label: PV-silenced mice responded to amphetamine exactly like controls, so PV interneurons are not needed for the PFC's control of psychostimulant sensitivity.
span.quote: However, PVIs do not seem to be required for this regulatory function of the PFC.

span.label: Local field potential recordings showed no enhanced synchronous activity after PV-cell silencing, ruling out epileptiform discharge as an explanation for the behavioural deficits.
span.quote: However, local field potential (LFP) recordings from PFC showed no indication of enhanced synchronous activity in PFC-PV-TeLC mice.

span.label: Applying the same tetanus-toxin silencing to somatostatin-expressing interneurons left working memory intact, showing the deficit is specific to the PV population.
span.quote: caused no change in working memory performance in the same task that was clearly impaired after inactivation of PVIs

span.label: The viral strategy expressed the toxin in over 75% of PV interneurons in prelimbic and infralimbic cortex, with only 4.3% off-target expression in PV-negative cells.
span.quote: Bilateral infusions of AAV-FLEX-TeLC resulted in expression of TeLC in over 75% of PVIs in prelimbic and infralimbic regions of the PFC ( Fig. 1C,D,F ).

span.label: VAMP2 immunoreactivity was strongly reduced in toxin-positive terminals compared with GFP-positive terminals, confirming the toxin cleaved its synaptic target.
span.quote: As expected, immunoreactivity for VAMP2 was strongly reduced in TeLC-positive terminals of PFC-PV-TeLC mice when compared with GFP-positive terminals of PFC-PV-GFP mice

span.label: both PV silencing and whole-region lesion increased repeat investigations in the hole-board test
span.quote: both PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion animals showed increased levels of repeat investigations (PFC-PV-TeLC vs. PFC-PV-GFP, p = 0.04; t = 1.97; PFC-Lesion vs. PFC-Saline, p = 0.04; t = 1.98)

span.label: spontaneous alternation fell from about 70% to about 57% after PV silencing
span.quote: This deficit was confirmed in a spontaneous alternation task in the Y-maze, where alternation levels were high in PFC-PV-GFP and PFC-Saline animals (70.0 ± 3.0% and 74.3 ± 4.1% respectively), but significantly lower in PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion animals (56.9

span.label: PV-silenced mice failed to improve in delayed match-to-place while controls did
span.quote: Whereas PFC-PV-GFP animals showed significant improvement in match trials, PFC-PV-TeLC animals did not

span.label: reversal learning was slowed by both manipulations, significantly so for PV silencing
span.quote: In contrast, during reversal, PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice needed more time to learn the new platform location although this was only significant for PFC-PV-TeLC mice (PFC-PV-TeLC vs. PFC-PV-GFP, day effect F(3,84) = 24; p < 0.001; group effect F(4,84) = 8.8; p = 0.006; and PFC-Lesion vs. PFC-Saline, F(3,60) = 2.1; p = 0.16)

span.label: the reversal deficit differed in severity: PV-silenced mice reached criterion with overtraining, over 30% of lesioned mice never did
span.quote: However, whereas PFC-PV-TeLC mice met reversal criterion upon overtraining, more than 30% of PFC-Lesion mice failed to do so.

span.label: lesioned mice showed no preference for a conspecific over an empty chamber, while PV-silenced mice did
span.quote: During sociability testing PFC-Lesion animals showed strongly reduced interaction with the conspecific animal ( p = 0.003; t = 3.57) ( Fig. 6B ). However, PFC-PV-TeLC mice displayed similar levels of social interaction as PFC-PV-GFP control animals

span.label: lesioned mice were hypersensitive to amphetamine; PV-silenced mice responded like controls
span.quote: In contrast, PFC-PV-TeLC animals did not differ from controls in amphetamine response (peak activity, t < 1; activity decay, t < 1)

span.label: the whole-region lesion produced deficits in all three symptom domains and PV silencing only in the cognitive one
span.quote: We found that PFC lesions produced behavioral alterations in all three symptom categories, whereas selective inactivation of PVIs caused deficits only in the cognitive domain.

span.label: CONTROL NULL: local field potentials showed no enhanced synchrony, so the deficits are not seizure activity from lost inhibition
span.quote: In principle, loss of PVI-mediated inhibition could induce hyper-activity in pyramidal cells and induce ictal discharges in the PFC, which in turn could complicate the interpretation of behavioral data. However, local field potential (LFP) recordings from PFC showed no indication of enhanced synchronous activity in PFC-PV-TeLC mice. PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-PV-GFP mice displayed similar absolute power at different spectral frequency bands

span.label: CONTROL NULL: neither manipulation altered locomotion or anxiety-related behaviour at baseline
span.quote: Neither PFC-PV-TeLC nor PFC-Lesion mice showed obvious neurological deficits or alterations in locomotion and anxiety-related behavior

span.label: CONTROL NULL: nose-poke counts were alike across groups, so the working memory deficit is not reduced exploration
span.quote: Although all groups of mice showed similar overall levels of nose pokes ( Fig. 2E,F ), indicating similar exploratory activity

span.label: CONTROL NULL: initial platform acquisition was normal in both perturbed groups, so the reversal deficit is not a spatial learning deficit
span.quote: During initial training PFC-PV-TeLC and PFC-Lesion mice learned the platform location as well as their respective controls as indicated by the reduction in path length (PFC-PV-TeLC/PFC-PV-GFP, day effect: F(4,120) = 45; p < 0.0001, no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1; PFC-Lesion/PFC-Saline, day effect: F(4,80) = 28; p < 0.0001; no effect with group as factor: F’s < 1) ( Fig. 4A,B ; see also Fig. 5 ) and the amount of time spent in the target quadrant during probe trials ( t’s < 1.4) ( Fig. 4 insets in A,B), indicating that spatial reference memory per se does not depend on the PFC

span.label: CONTROL NULL: silencing somatostatin interneurons the same way left working memory intact
span.quote: Such a “division of labor” scenario between different populations of interneurons is further supported by our finding that analogous tetanus toxin-based targeting of a different, somatostatin (Sst)-expressing, population of interneurons in the PFC of Sst-Cre mice 71 caused no change in working memory performance in the same task that was clearly impaired after inactivation of PVIs

span.label: PV-silenced mice kept the preference for social novelty that lesioned mice lost
span.quote: Accordingly social approach/avoidance behavior as well as social recognition memory/novelty preference depends on the PFC circuitry. PV-positive interneurons, however, do not seem to be a crucial component of this circuit.

span.label: behavioral flexibility
span.quote: Behavioral flexibility, which permits the individual to appropriate behavioral strategies to a changing environment, is another core function of the PFC that is impaired in schizophrenia
